key_insight: A symmetry-preserving linear-attention mechanism gives machine-learning force fields global, long-range awareness at linear computational cost, enabling scalable modeling of interactions across entire molecular systems.
problem_solved: Efficiently modeling long-range interactions in ML force fields without resorting to costly quadratic attention, fragmentation heuristics, or ad-hoc physics fixes.
method: Design a linear-attention kernel that aggregates global messages in O(N) time while avoiding pairwise quadratic complexity.
Integrate the linear-attention module into ML force-field architectures while preserving physical symmetries (e.g., equivariance/invariance).
Provide a flexible, plug-in alternative to fragmentation-based and physics-based long-range modules, with empirical validation on molecular dynamics tasks.
impact: Enables scalable, symmetry-aware ML force fields for larger molecules and longer simulations, reducing compute and simplifying model design for practitioners working on materials and biomolecular modeling.
visual_elements: Schematic of model pipeline showing local encoder + linear-attention global module and outputs (forces/energies).
Complexity chart comparing O(N) linear attention vs O(N^2) standard attention as system size grows.
Molecular visualization illustrating capture of long-range interactions (e.g., distant charge effects) with and without the new module.
Bar/line plot comparing accuracy and runtime against fragmentation and physics-based long-range baselines.
paper_title: Linear attention goes global in molecular dynamics
